{{nihongo|'''Obusuma Shrine'''|小被神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

'''Obusuma Shrine''' (おぶすまじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located along the {{ill|Arakawa River (Kantō)|Q625465|qid=Q625465}} in {{ill|Obusuma|Q11578176|qid=Q11578176|lt=Obusuma Village}}, {{ill|Yorii, Saitama|arz|يورى|ca|Yorii|ceb|Yorii Machi|de|Yorii (Saitama)|eo|Jorii|es|Yorii|fa|یوریی، سایتاما|fr|Yorii|id|Yorii, Saitama|it|Yorii|ja|寄居町|ko|요리이정|mg|Yorii|ms|Yorii, Saitama|pl|Yorii|ro|Yorii, Saitama|ru|Йории|sv|Yorii|tl|Yorii, Saitama|tr|Yorii|uk|Йорії (Сайтама)|ur|یوری، سائتاما|zh|寄居町|qid=Q961604}}, {{ill|Ōsato District, Saitama|Q1075196|qid=Q1075196}}, {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|Q128186|qid=Q128186}}. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Q1056017|qid=Q1056017|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto}}. It is a Shikinaisha (listed shrine) of {{ill|Musashi Province|Q907398|qid=Q907398}}{{ill|Obusuma district|Q11578175|qid=Q11578175}}. Its former shrine rank was village shrine.

=== History ===
According to tradition, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Ankan|Q241765|qid=Q241765}} (531–535), Tomita Shika built a small shrine in Tsukagoshi, Tomita Village (present-day grounds of Daishōzan Shingon-in Fudō-ji Temple) and enshrined the Obusuma deity there.<ref name="社頭掲示板">From the shrine notice board</ref>

In the 9th year of {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} ({{ill|1669|Q7602|qid=Q7602}}), due to a territorial boundary dispute between villagers of Tomita and villagers of Akahama—who had relocated there after the great flood of the Arakawa River in the 8th year of {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|ckb|تێنشۆ (سەردەمی مۆمۆیاما)|fa|تنشو|fr|Ère Tenshō (Momoyama)|ja|天正|ko|덴쇼 (아즈치모모야마 시대)|ro|Era Tenshō (Momoyama)|ru|Тэнсё (Адзути-Момояма)|simple|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|sr|Теншо (Момојама период)|sv|Tenshō|tr|Tenshō (Momoyama)|zh|天正 (日本)|qid=Q1145058}} ({{ill|1580|Q6712|qid=Q6712}})—the shrine was moved to its current location.<ref name="武州男衾郡上下富田村与赤浜村境論之事">From “Bushū Obusuma-gun Kamishimo Tomita-mura to Akahama-mura Boundary Dispute”</ref>

With the beginning of the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}, due to the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535|lt=separation of Shinto and Buddhism edict}}, the monk of the affiliated temple “Fudō-ji” returned to lay life and became a Shinto priest of the shrine.<ref name="新編武蔵風土記稿">From “Newly Compiled Musashi Fudoki”</ref>

=== Shrine status ===
==== Divine rank ====
* 9 March, 1st year of {{ill|Genji era|Q1325419|qid=Q1325419}} ({{ill|1864|Q7704|qid=Q7704}}) – Senior First Rank<ref name="宗源宣旨">From “Sōgen Senji”</ref>

==== Modern shrine ranking system ====
* November 11, Meiji 4 – Village shrine
* July 1, Meiji 41 – Shrine receiving offerings of sacred food and paper streamers

=== Enshrined deities ===
* (Main deity) Ninigi-no-Mikoto
* (Associated deities) Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto, Hikohohodemi-no-Mikoto<ref name="社頭掲示板">From the shrine notice board</ref>
